title: Microsoft Stock: Buy or Sell? (My Final Verdict)
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA updates Microsoft after its quarterly results and upgrades the stock to a buying opportunity, reversing the downgrade he made a few weeks earlier when the price ran from $350 to $550 between July and October. Shares now trade at $529. The centrepiece is remaining performance obligations of $677 billion - contracted cloud revenue, with roughly 30% (about $225 billion) recognised in the next 12 months over a 2.3-year weighted average duration - though a large share comes from OpenAI, and fears that OpenAI may delay or not pay its obligations have ebbed and flowed; Anthropic's narrowing losses and a possible OpenAI IPO would ease that concern. On the weak side, Windows OEM revenue fell 27% year on year on soft PC demand and elevated channel inventory, with management expecting declines to worsen - the same higher memory and CPU prices driving AI demand are hurting consumer electronics. At a forward P/E of 22, slightly below its average since early 2024, his updated discounted cash flow model gives a higher fair value, about 11.4% above the market price after a margin of safety (the exact fair-value figure is garbled in the captions). He upgraded Microsoft to BUY on 29 October 2026 with medium conviction, and now records the date of each rating change in his spreadsheets.

calls.base_case: Contracted cloud backlog converts steadily (2.3-year weighted average duration); AI segments boom while PC/Windows/gaming stay soft for a few quarters.
